description: promote_last_2 (DECtalk 4.63 ph_aloph.c:1689-1722): a stressed syllabic before a verb phrase, at the last stress before a clause-level boundary or with a delayed hat fall pending, gives primary stress to the last secondary-stressed syllabic of the first stretch after it that has one. A stretch ends at a boundary of the comma value or more, which a kept prepositional-phrase start leaves on the phone before it. "Boys for" sets the delayed fall, so "men" before the verb makes the call although primary stresses follow.

entries.text: Boys for men asked for it.
Boys for men went for it when he had it then.
Boys for men asked for it when he had it then.
Boys for men asked for it when he had it.
Boys and men asked for it when he had it then.
Boys for men asked for them then when he had it.
Boys for men asked for it then went for it when he had it.
Boys for men went for it when he asked for it then.
Boys for men asked for it if he had it when he went.
Men for boys ran to it for him then.
